name: Hortobágy National Park
tagline: The puszta, Central Europe's largest grassland, with horsemen, grey cattle, racka sheep, migrating cranes and the longest stone bridge in Hungary.
highlight: Riding horsemen across the open puszta at sunset under a huge sky.
shortDescription: Hungary's oldest national park and a UNESCO cultural landscape, with the Nine-Hole Bridge, horse shows, traditional herding, birdwatching and crane migration.
metaDescription: A Hortobágy National Park travel guide: the puszta, Nine-Hole Bridge, horse shows, herdsmen, birdwatching, crane migration, gulyás, how to get there and a one-day plan.

image.alt: Horses on the open grassland of the Hortobágy puszta

intro: The puszta is the Great Hungarian Plain, an enormous grassland stretching across eastern Hungary. Hortobágy National Park, founded in 1973, protects 800 square kilometres of it, and is Hungary's largest protected area. The landscape is flat and vast, with grasses, wetlands, fish ponds and a vast sky, and it has been shaped by centuries of grazing by cattle, horses and sheep. UNESCO lists it as a cultural landscape.

The traditional life of the puszta is still on show. Herdsmen, called csikós when they tend horses, ride in a distinctive costume of blue shirts, wide trousers and hats, and perform horse shows in which riders control teams of five horses at a gallop. Curly-horned Racka sheep and long-horned Hungarian grey cattle graze, and the stone Nine-Hole Bridge, the longest in Hungary at 167 metres, dates from 1833.

For nature lovers, the park is a major bird area. In October, tens of thousands of common cranes stop here on their migration, and visitors also see spoonbills, great bustards and many others. The park is a day trip from Debrecen or Tokaj, or a stop on a road trip east of Budapest.

whyVisit.intro: Hortobágy is the best place to see traditional Hungarian rural life and wide open landscapes.
